structure: California History-Social Science Framework (2016), a 855-page K-12 framework. Front matter (cover, publishing info, contents, foreword, acknowledgments) then Chapter 1 Introduction and Chapter 2 'Instructional Practice K-Grade Five' (running header 'K-Grade Five' on each page; contains Disciplinary Thinking and Analysis Skills, literacy, ELD, research guidance). Chapters 3-8 are grade chapters (Kindergarten, Grade One ... Grade Five), each opening with a chapter/grade title, bulleted guiding questions (extracted as 'n' bullet units and wrapped lines), an overview, then unit narratives headed by topic subheadings (each keyed to content standards such as K.1, 1.4, 5.6) with guiding questions, plus 'Grade X Classroom Example' boxes (title, ELA/ELD strategy, 'Example (continued)' on following pages, ending in a 'CA HSS Content Standard / CA CCSS / CA ELD' citation line). The formal content standards text is not in this range; it is in Appendix C later in the document. Within this range, grade chapters are narrative description of what students study, so labeled examples with the chapter grade. Running headers give chapter number. Table cells appear only inside classroom examples (ELD table in Ch2; classroom constitution organizer in Ch6; Preamble sentence-deconstruction tables in Ch8). Range ends at u1272 which does not exist in the view; last unit in range is u1271 (Grade Five 'Life in the Young Republic', page 135).
